chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jamilyah, from Jabir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever conceals a testimony, or testifies with it to shed the blood of a Muslim or to divert the wealth of a Muslim, will come on the Day of Resurrection with a darkness extending as far as the eye can see before his face, and with a dullness in his face that all creatures will recognize by his name and lineage.'

And whoever testifies with a true testimony to revive the right of a Muslim, will come on the Day of Resurrection with a light extending as far as the eye can see before his face, that all creatures will recognize by his name and lineage.'
Then Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not see that God the Exalted says:
And establish the testimony for God
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual consequences of concealing or misusing testimony in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) emphasizes the eschatological weight of judicial testimony, linking physical appearance on Judgment Day to the integrity of one’s witness. It highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the moral and spiritual dimensions of legal evidence, where truthful testimony is an act of preserving life and property, while misuse leads to divine obscurity. The concluding Quranic verse reinforces that establishing testimony is ultimately an act of worship and obedience to God.
